en: And even when someone says, well, RAG isn't dead, like Jerry, the CEO of LlamaIndex, they still have to kill something, and apparently this something is chunking.
zh: 甚至当有人说「RAG 没死」,比如 LlamaIndex 的 CEO Jerry,他们还是得干掉某个东西,而显然这个东西就是分块。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, don't invest in it, don't do it.

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is the reason that people said that chunking is dead, because everybody's using agentic search now, right?

speaker: Unknown
en: You have greps, you have ls, you have finds.

speaker: Unknown
en: All of these are great.

en: But these are still not enough if you have a lot of data and you have various amount of queries.

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a second.
zh: 稍等一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the main reason that a lot of people don't like to talk about chunking is because it's not the fun part.
zh: 我认为很多人不喜欢谈分块的主要原因,是因为它不是有趣的那部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: In every RAG or files system, we have two stages.
zh: 在每个 RAG 或文件系统里,我们有两个阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first stage is the boring one, as you may, the one you do in the beginning.

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a lot of data.

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to preprocess it.

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to decide on the chunk size.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have to store everything in a vector DB.

speaker: Unknown
en: The other part is the retrieval part, essentially the one that happens per query.
zh: 另一部分是检索部分,基本上是每次查询时发生的那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is something which is much easier to do, right?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's much easier to optimize.

speaker: Unknown
en: You can use all your queries and then you can play with the max K, top K, sorry, you can play with the hybrid search maybe, those kind of things.

speaker: Unknown
en: Much more fun to do retrieval tuning, right?

speaker: Unknown
en: So I will claim that if we have to kill something, if something has to be dead, then it's probably retrieval tuning.

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, agentic search probably killed that.
zh: 是的,智能体搜索可能已经把它干掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, but still, IgenticSearch, even if we can accept the fact that it killed retrieval tuning, it's still not good enough when you have a lot of, right, scale, a lot of data.
zh: 而且,不过,IgenticSearch,即使我们能接受它干掉了检索调优这个事实,当你有很多,对吧,规模、大量数据时,它仍然不够好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It costs a lot of money.
zh: 它花费很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I have to mention that anymore.
zh: 我想我不必再提这个了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Token maxing is, like, something that everybody's talking about.
zh: Token 消耗最大化是,比如,大家都在谈论的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing underneath, which is if the data itself is not ordered in a right way,
zh: 而底下的问题在于,如果数据本身没有以正确的方式组织,

speaker: Unknown
en: In your folders, in your directories, you still get something which is inefficient.

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's try to think of a timely example, right?

en: The FIFA World Cup is now.

speaker: Unknown

en: So every directory is, let's say, the 98 one, the 2002 one, and so on, and so on.

speaker: Unknown
en: But if your query asks,
zh: 但如果你的查询问的是,

en: Which team won the most World Cups?
zh: 哪支球队赢得的世界杯最多?

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't just go to a folder and ask that.

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to go to every folder, see who won, and then aggregate this together, which is very inefficient.
zh: 你必须去每一个文件夹,看谁赢了,然后把这些汇总起来,这是非常低效的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer, by the way, is Brazil, I hope, at least according to the time that this conversation's happening.
zh: 顺便说一下,答案是巴西,我希望,至少根据这场对话发生的时间来看。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, retrieval doesn't actually die.
zh: 所以,检索其实并没有死。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, we're not killing anything in this lecture.
zh: 好的，在这节课里我们不会砍掉任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is got devoted into plumbing.
zh: 它完全 devoted( dedicated / dedicated ) 到管道工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that everybody who worked on any rug system know the feeling.
zh: 我认为每一个做过任何 RAG 系统的人都知道那种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Day one or week one or maybe even month one, if you're very thorough, you're picking some sort of a chunk size.
zh: 第一天、第一周，或者如果你非常仔细的话甚至第一个月，你在挑选某种 chunk 大小。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say 512.
zh: 比如说 512。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe you're probably putting some overlap, right, 10%, 20%, so on, indexing everything and forget all about it.
zh: 然后也许你可能加一些 overlap,对吧，10%、20% 等等，把所有东西都建立索引，然后就把它全忘了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can, right, we talk a lot about the fixed chunking strategies where if your chunk is something which is too big, right, so you get the whole picture, which is nice, but you're losing a lot of the nuance and all the chunks will not get meaningful embeddings.
zh: 你确实可以这样做，对吧，我们聊了很多固定 chunking 策略，如果你的 chunk 太大，对吧，你能得到全貌，这很好，但你丢失了很多细微差别，而且所有 chunk 都不会得到有意义的 embedding。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where if you will choose your chunks to be too small, you're getting the big picture lost.
zh: 而如果你把 chunk 选得太小，你就会丢失大局。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really it won't be as efficient.
zh: 而且它确实不会那么高效。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what this tells us is that chunking is essentially a lossy compression.
zh: 所以这告诉我们的是，chunking 本质上是一种有损压缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: No matter what we're doing, we're losing something.
zh: 无论我们做什么，我们都在丢失一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I will claim that there is no right chunk size.
zh: 而我要声称，不存在正确的 chunk 大小。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of you who worked on data will say, no, but we have this corpus, we have this data set, and we really used and we optimized our system to work very, very well on this data.
zh: 你们很多做过数据的人会说，不，但我们有这个语料库，我们有这个数据集，我们真的用过，而且我们优化了我们的系统，让它在这个数据上跑得非常非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we thought so, too.
zh: 我们也曾这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had a lot of experience with it, with a lot of different types of agents and systems and workflows that you can really, and right, you think about benchmarks, how easy it is to overfit your model to a benchmark.
zh: 我们在这方面有很多经验，见过很多不同类型的智能体、系统和工作流，你真的可以，对吧，你想想 benchmarks,把你的模型过拟合到某个 benchmark 上是多么容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: But not with RAG.
zh: 但 RAG 不是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't happen there.
zh: 在 RAG 上这种事不会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you cannot really optimize it per dataset, and I will claim that it is query-dependent.
zh: 你无法真正针对每个数据集进行优化，而我要声称它是依赖于查询的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how can I be so sure?

speaker: Unknown
en: How can I claim such a thing?
zh: 我怎么敢声称这种事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we ran experiments, and we tested, and now I'm going to present it to you.

en: So what we did, instead of saying what is the best chunk size per data, let's find out.

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's actually take a data set and duplicate this data set several times.

speaker: Unknown
en: In this case, six times.

speaker: Unknown
en: In every duplication, in every instance, the chunk size is different.
zh: 在每一次复制、每一个实例中，chunk 大小都不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have a database with a chunk size of 2,000, a database with a chunk size of 1,000, and so on, and so on.
zh: 所以我们有一个 chunk 大小为 2000 的数据库，一个 chunk 大小为 1000 的数据库，以此类推，等等等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did it with several datasets, so QMSUM, which is a meeting transcript dataset, narrative QA, which is question answering on novels, and Seinfeld dataset, which is a trivia about nothing, not really, it's trivia questions about the transcripts of Seinfeld.
zh: 我们用几个数据集做了这件事，有 QMSUM,这是一个会议转写数据集；有 narrative QA,这是一个对小说做问答的数据集；还有一个 Seinfeld 数据集，这是一个“关于无事的冷知识”，其实不是，它是关于 Seinfeld 剧本转写的冷知识问答。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of a trolling dataset that we build in-house.
zh: 这是一个我们内部构建的、有点恶搞性质的数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also published it if anybody wants the link at the end.
zh: 我们也把它公开发布了，如果有人想要链接的话，在最后。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we tested on all of them.
zh: 我们在所有这些数据集上做了测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: to see what happens.
zh: 看看会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And first of all, we just wanted to see, for every dataset, which chunk size is the best.
zh: 首先呢，我们只是想看看，对于每个数据集，哪个 chunk 大小是最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we're seeing here is an example from the Seinfeld dataset, where essentially two queries, which are different by nature,
zh: 而我们在这里看到的是来自 Seinfeld 数据集的一个例子，本质上两个查询，它们性质不同，

speaker: Unknown
en: Get different results based on that chunk size.
zh: 基于 chunk 大小的不同得到了不同的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first question, what is the name for Jerry's favorite shirt?
zh: 那么第一个问题，Jerry 最喜欢的衬衫叫什么名字？

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see this is a very focused question, very specific question.
zh: 你可以看到这是一个非常聚焦的问题，非常具体的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer to it is probably very contained.
zh: 它的答案很可能是非常集中的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is something that a smaller chunk size will do best in.
zh: 这是更小的 chunk 大小会表现最好的那种问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see rank one versus rank below 50.
zh: 你可以看到 rank one 对比 rank 50 以下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Between 100 tokens fixed.
zh: 在 100 tokens 固定之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: chunk size to 100.
zh: chunk 大小设为 100。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas a question like who does Jerry describe as his nemesis and pure evil, which I'm not even that big of a Seinfeld fan, and I know it's Newman, but if you look at the transcript, it's not something you can find that easily.
zh: 而像“Jerry 把谁描述为他的宿敌和纯粹的邪恶”这样的问题，我甚至不算是个特别铁杆的 Seinfeld 粉，我也知道是 Newman,但如果你去看剧本转写，这不是一个能轻易找到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can see that it really changes, right?
zh: 你可以看到它真的会变化，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you use small chunk size, you will not get the answer.
zh: 如果你用小的 chunk 大小，你得不到答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we did to really, after we ran all of these things and we've noticed that, we said, what if we had an oracle or a genie, if you want, that can tell us for every query what is the best chunk size to do retrieval for?
zh: 而在跑完所有这些东西并注意到这一点之后，我们做了什么，我们说，如果我们有一个 oracle 或者说一个精灵，能为每个查询告诉我们做检索用哪个 chunk 大小最好，那会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: This essentially is the Oracle experiment.

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what we wanted to know to see the potential.
zh: 这就是我们想知道的，为了看到潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We already have the answers, so we're not actually building a system here.
zh: 我们已经有答案了，所以我们并不是真的在这里构建一个系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just want to see what is the potential that we have here.
zh: 我们只是想看看我们这里拥有的潜力是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what you can see here in this graph, first of all, the y-axis is the recall.
zh: 而你在这张图里能看到的，首先，y 轴是 recall。

speaker: Unknown
en: Higher is better.
zh: 越高越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The x-axis is the number of retrieved chunks, so it's recall at k versus k. You can see all the blue lines.
zh: 横轴是检索到的块的数量，所以就是 recall at k 对 k 的曲线。你可以看到所有这些蓝色的线。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably indistinguishable, but each of them is the performance for a fixed chunk size, whereas the orange one is the Oracle line.
zh: 它们可能难以区分，但每一条都是固定块大小下的性能，而橙色的那条是 Oracle 线。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is, for every query, we took the best one out of these.
zh: 也就是说，对每一个查询，我们从这些里面取了最好的那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see it happens across several datasets.

speaker: Unknown
en: In a lot of them, you can actually see that the blue lines intersect with each other, meaning that indeed for a lot of the datasets, no chunk size actually dominates.

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's more interesting is that there's a lot of potential.
zh: 更有意思的是，这里有很大的潜力。

speaker: Unknown
en: The gap, which you can see between the orange line and all the blue lines, is big.
zh: 你可以看到橙色线和所有蓝线之间的这个差距，是很大的。

en: And when I say big, it's something like 20 to 40 percent
zh: 我说很大，是指大概 20% 到 40%

speaker: Unknown
en: Just from doing strategy on chunking, and very simple strategy, may I add.

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is, like, this gap, this is what the choice of 512 or 1,000 or whatever, right?

en: This number is just arbitrary.

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what it costs you.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the problem here is
zh: 而我认为这里的问题在于

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bit tricky because it's kind of like an information problem that we don't have the information that we need at every stage.
zh: 这有点棘手，因为它有点像一个信息问题：我们在每个阶段都没有我们所需的信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what do I mean by that?
zh: 我这是什么意思呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm looking at the indexing part, where I do have control over the chunk size, I don't know what the queries will be.
zh: 如果我看的是索引这一部分，在这一步我确实能控制块大小，但我不知道查询会是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can guess, I can maybe estimate, I can try, but I don't know what the queries will be, so I cannot adjust my chunk size accordingly.

speaker: Unknown
en: And the retrieval part where I do have my queries, I cannot control the chunk size, right?
zh: 而在检索这一部分，我手上确实有查询，但我无法控制块大小，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's already fixed.
zh: 它已经固定了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I obviously will not do the entire process per query from the beginning.
zh: 而且我显然不会为每个查询从头执行整个流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we looked at prior works such as notably Anthropic, Contextual Retrieval, where they enrich every chunk, and others that essentially try to improve the latent space of every chunk, but this is not the direction that we went.

speaker: Unknown
en: All of them just stayed in the model of let's work with a fixed chunk size, whereas we took a different approach, and we said, why commit to one where we can commit to several?
zh: 它们都停留在固定块大小的模式里，而我们采取了不同的做法，我们说：既然可以选定多个，为什么要只选定一个呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And we call it the multiscale indexing.

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially, we're just doing what we've seen before, so we're checking the database, we duplicate it and chunk it with several

speaker: Unknown
en: Chunk sizes or window sizes.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, sorry, and then, this is what happens at the indexing, and then at retrieval time, we are querying all of them.

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we had N duplicates of the database, N window sizes, we now have to run six different retrieval calls per query.

speaker: Unknown
en: Sorry, six as N.

en: And how do we combine them?
zh: 那我们怎么把它们结合起来呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: We obviously cannot use the Oracle, right?
zh: 我们显然不能使用 Oracle，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The Oracle is something that we have just for potential.
zh: Oracle 只是我们用来衡量潜力的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: In real life, we don't know the answer.

en: But what we can do is to find some sort of merging algorithm.

en: Now, you would say, when we look at it like this, what can be the issue?

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that we have N ranking, but the rankings are for chunks.
zh: 问题在于我们手上有 N 个排名，但这些排名是针对块的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And chunks with different sizes are not really comparable, right?
zh: 而不同大小的块其实是没有可比性的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So instead, we opted to do something which is pretty popular these days, and a lot of the RAG systems actually work like this, that instead of just retrieving the chunk,
zh: 所以，我们选择了做一件现在相当流行的事，很多 RAG 系统实际上就是这样工作的：不是只检索块，

speaker: Unknown
en: When we're getting a chunk, we're retrieving the entire document.
zh: 而是当我们拿到一个块时，我们检索整个文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: When context window grows, we want to give more and more context.
zh: 随着上下文窗口变大，我们想给越来越多的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now, in this case, we have N rankings of the same documents because they're not chunks anymore.
zh: 这样一来，在这个情况下，我们就有对同一批文档的 N 个排名，因为它们不再是块了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this, we can compare.
zh: 而这个，我们就可以比较了。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this case, you can think of retrieval as essentially just voting.
zh: 在这种情况下，你可以把检索本质上就理解为投票。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pure re-ranking.
zh: 纯粹的重排序。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have run ranking, and then we're doing it re-rank.
zh: 我们不是先做一次排名然后再做重排。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're having N different ranks of the relevant documents, and we want to aggregate them all into one.
zh: 我们有 N 个不同排序的相关文档,我们想把它们全部聚合为一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why we are using something called RRF, Reciprocal Rank Fusion, which is pretty much a simple formula.
zh: 这就是为什么我们使用一种叫 RRF 的东西，Reciprocal Rank Fusion(倒数排名融合)，它基本上就是一个简单的公式。

speaker: Unknown
en: We tried several things.
zh: 我们试了好几种方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: This worked the best.
zh: 这个效果最好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as you can see, it's not a model.
zh: 而且你可以看到，它不是一个模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not something that you have to do specifically.
zh: 这不是你需要专门去做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially, this is just a simple script that takes really no time.
zh: 特别是，这只是一个简单的脚本，几乎不需要花什么时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is how the full system looks like.
zh: 这就是整个系统的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have the indexing n times, then we query each query from every database, and we are using RRF to combine them all.
zh: 所以我们做 n 次索引，然后我们从每个数据库查询每一个 query,并且我们使用 RRF 来把它们全部结合起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the results, you can guess that they're good, otherwise I would not be standing here and being way too much confident.
zh: 至于结果，你可以猜到它们很好，否则我不会站在这里，还表现得这么自信过头。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can see we tested across several datasets, QMSum, NarrativeQA, Seinfeld, and also FinanceBench.
zh: 但你可以看到，我们在几个数据集上做了测试，QMSum、NarrativeQA、Seinfeld,还有 FinanceBench。

speaker: Unknown
en: We took all of them, and it matches the best, or beats the best fixed size.
zh: 我们把它们全都拿来了，它 matches 最好的，或者说打败了最好的固定尺寸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's see it in a graph.
zh: 让我们用一张图来看。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bit hard to see here, so I'll walk it slowly.
zh: 这里有点不太容易看清，所以我会慢慢讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every row here is chunk size, so you can see 50, 100, and so on.
zh: 这里的每一行是 chunk size,你可以看到 50、100 等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bottom row is our method, this one, the one that you do from all of them and then combine, and every column is recall at something.
zh: 最下面一行是我们的方法，就是这一个，从所有这些里做然后再结合起来的那个，每一列是某个 recall at 指标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So recall at one, two, three, up until 10.
zh: 也就是 recall at 1、2、3,一直到 10。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you can see here is that two things, right?
zh: 你在这里能看到的是两件事，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, that across recall at whatever, our method still wins, which you can think is very easy, but the fact that you have to combine all of them is not something which is very trivial.
zh: 首先，无论 recall at 几，我们的方法仍然获胜，你可能觉得这很容易，但你必须把它们全部结合起来这件事并不是很 trivial 的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also you can see that the quality actually increases.
zh: 另外你还可以看到，质量实际上在提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: The heat map where you can see it's become much greener.
zh: 热力图你可以看到它变得更绿了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, this was just something that I wanted to show in large.
zh: 再说一次，这只是我想放大展示的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here you can see all four of the data sets.
zh: 在这里你可以看到全部四个数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where we do achieve better results, really quite like 20, 30, 40% even in a lot of the things.
zh: 我们确实取得了更好的结果，在很多项上真的达到了 20、30、40% 甚至更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, there are results that I did not show you here which are on MTab.
zh: 还有一些结果我在这里没有展示，是在 MTab 上的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can see in our blog, I will put the link later, we're getting there also a lot of improvements, somewhere between 10 to 40% depending on the data set.
zh: 你可以看我们的博客，我稍后会放链接，我们在那里也得到了很多提升，根据数据集不同大约在 10 到 40% 之间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I'm not naive.
zh: 现在，我不是天真的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not going to claim here that this costs nothing.
zh: 我不会在这里声称这是零成本的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, there is a cost, right?
zh: 显然，是有成本的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: No free launches.
zh: 没有免费的午餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything has to come with something.

speaker: Unknown
en: And yes, this costs with extra memory.
zh: 是的，这带来的成本是额外的内存。

speaker: Unknown
en: It costs something between 2 to 5 to 0 of 1, right?
zh: 它的成本是 2 到 5 到 0 of 1 之间的某个东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: A constant of additional memory where you have to keep all of those copies of the database.
zh: 一个额外的内存常数，你必须保留所有那些数据库的副本。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, if you think about it, latency-wise, it doesn't really affect that because you can do all the retrieval part parallelly and also the RRF part doesn't really take a lot of time.
zh: 不过，如果你想一想，在延迟方面，它其实并没有太大影响，因为你可以把所有检索部分并行执行，而且 RRF 部分也不怎么花时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will say that this was a very nice research project that we did and we got really, really cool results.
zh: 我想说，这是我们做的一个非常不错的研究项目，我们得到了真的、真的很酷的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are things to do, right?
zh: 还有事情要做，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are places to improve.
zh: 有可以改进的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are future work to do.
zh: 有未来的工作要做。

speaker: Unknown
en: More precisely, we want to understand how many chunk sizes do we want and which.
zh: 更具体地说，我们想理解我们需要多少个 chunk size,以及是哪些。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that we worked with 50, 100, 200, and so on was pretty arbitrary, to be honest, so we do need to figure out how to compute this and how to know how many copies exactly do you need.
zh: 说实话，我们使用 50、100、200 等等这个事实是相当随意的，所以我们确实需要弄清楚如何计算这个，以及如何确切知道你需要多少个副本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also go beyond RRF.
zh: 还有超越 RRF。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that we're using RRF is because it worked the best from the methods that we used, but it doesn't mean that there is no better method.
zh: 我们使用 RRF 是因为它在我们用过的方法里效果最好，但这并不意味着没有更好的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if I need to leave you with something, I would say that agents didn't kill retrieval.
zh: 如果我需要给你们留下一句话，我会说智能体并没有杀死检索。

en: Nothing died, come on.
zh: 什么都没有死，拜托。

en: Again, without any, something too sophisticated.
zh: 再说一次，不需要任何太复杂的东西。

zh: 那里还有一个示例代码和 Seinfeld 数据集。

zh: 就这些了。
